event.title: Macron Implements Measures Against Intensifying Russian Hybrid Threats
event.canonical_title: Macron Implements Measures Against Intensifying Russian Hybrid Threats
event.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron has ordered protective measures for the country's critical infrastructure and defense industry in response to escalating Russian hybrid attacks. This announcement followed a meeting with political party leaders to discuss the growing threats from Russia, particularly in light of recent developments in Europe. Macron emphasized that the hybrid threat from Moscow has intensified in recent weeks, necessitating immediate action.

timeline.title: Ukraine Launches Major Drone Attack on Moscow During Russian Elections
timeline.summary: Ukraine has launched over 1,000 drones at Russia, marking the largest drone attack on Moscow to date. The assault coincided with the final day of Russia's parliamentary elections, resulting in at least two fatalities and numerous injuries in the Moscow region. Damage was reported at an oil refinery and a residential building, as local officials confirmed the scale of the attack.
key_facts: Ukraine fired over 1,000 drones at Russia, including hundreds targeting Moscow.
The attack resulted in at least two deaths and 20 injuries.
Significant damage occurred at an oil refinery and a residential building in Moscow.

event_overview.title: About Russian Hybrid Attacks
event_overview.subject: Russian Hybrid Attacks
event_overview.summary: Russian hybrid attacks is a term used by European and NATO institutions for coordinated hostile activity attributed to Russia that falls below conventional armed conflict, including cyberattacks, sabotage, interference in democratic processes, and information manipulation. In France, the issue combines domestic protection of critical infrastructure and cyberspace with efforts to detect foreign digital interference in public debate.

facts.label: Threat scope
facts.value: The EU identifies sabotage, disruption of critical infrastructure, cyberattacks, foreign information manipulation and interference, and attempts to undermine democracy and electoral processes as forms of Russia-linked hybrid activity.

facts.label: European legal framework
facts.value: The Council of the European Union adopted Regulation (EU) 2024/2642 on 8 October 2024, creating targeted restrictive measures in response to Russia’s destabilising activities; the framework provides for asset freezes and bans on making funds or economic resources available to listed persons or entities.

facts.label: French foreign-interference capability
facts.value: France created VIGINUM by Decree No. 2021-922 of 13 July 2021. Attached to the General Secretariat for Defence and National Security, it detects and characterises foreign digital interference affecting France’s public debate.

facts.label: French response focus
facts.value: On 18 September 2026, the French presidency said authorities had raised vigilance toward Russian hybrid attacks and were preparing protection for critical infrastructure and sensitive defence-industrial sites against drone and cyber attacks, alongside measures against foreign interference.

facts.label: Alliance approach
facts.value: NATO treats countering hybrid threats as a resilience and collective-security task that includes critical-infrastructure protection, strategic communications, cyber defence, energy security, civil preparedness, and support to allies.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the September 18–20, 2026 developments involving France’s response and a major drone attack during Russian elections; it does not attempt to catalogue every alleged Russian hybrid operation, cyber incident, sanction, or development in the wider war in Ukraine.
